faq.q: Can I get sole and heel photos from a single side shot?
faq.a: Not reliably. The result can only show details visible in your upload. For a tread or heel view, start from a separate photo of the outsole or heel instead of a side shot.

faq.q: Does this work for Amazon main images for shoes?
faq.a: For a main image, use the shoe alone on a pure white background, filling most of the frame, with no props or text. Add size charts and width notes to gallery images instead.

faq.q: Can I show the logo of a sneaker brand I resell?
faq.a: Requests built around a logo or trademark you don't own may be declined. If you resell branded pairs, your own straight product photos are the safer choice for those listings.

faq.q: What angles should I shoot for shoe ads?
faq.a: Start with one full side profile, then add a top view and a sole or heel shot. Those three views answer fit, shape and tread questions without asking the generated image to invent details it cannot see.

faq.q: Can one shoe photo produce both a listing image and a walking video?
faq.a: Yes. A clear side-profile photo can become a white background or lifestyle still and also feed a short stride video. Keep the full toe, heel and collar visible so the reframe does not crop the shape.

faq.q: How do I avoid a branded look when selling unbranded shoes?
faq.a: Start from a photo of a plain, unbranded pair and check the result for stripes, sole shapes, or stitching that echoes a known logo. Keep logos and text out of both the source photo and the finished scene.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid footwear ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded clips are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid ads and product videos. Keep comfort and performance claims to verified facts, and pass the platform's ad review.

faq.q: Is an AI on-foot clip different from hiring a UGC creator?
faq.a: Yes. You upload one photo and pay credits per clip instead of a creator fee, sample shipping, and usage terms. The person is generated and not a real reviewer, so present the video as an ad.
